No return of BTAL, any managed-futures fund, MERFX, daily IEF/TLT or any seasonal split was looked at this session. T5 and T6 reuse 2013-2026, a window Step 340 already read for the AQR trend factor and DBMF; that is declared, not hidden.
owner_approval: 2026-11-11, brief docs/FRESH_EYES_STRATEGY_SEARCH_PROMPT.md pasted in chat: 'Go through the ranked list one idea at a time... Pre-register it in 2.0/config/ before touching any return data'
why_this_exists: Phase 3 of the fresh-eyes brief left six ideas that are not in PROJECT_HISTORY.md or the queue's Closed table and need no paid data. Everything else on the 42-item Phase 1 list is already closed, already on a clock, or blocked on data (see docs/FRESH_EYES_REVIEW_V2.md).

common.benchmark: static_spy_gld_shy_v1: equal thirds SPY/GLD/SHY, reset at the test's own cadence
common.cash: BIL total return from 2007-06, Fama-French daily RF compounded before that
common.significance: paired circular block bootstrap of the Sharpe difference, 5000 draws, block 12 months (26 weeks for weekly data), null centred at zero, one-sided
common.alpha: 0.05 / 6 = 0.0083 (Bonferroni over this registry's six trials). The project's cumulative search is in the hundreds of trials on overlapping data, so even a pass here is a research candidate for a forward clock, never 'ready'.
common.prices: Yahoo adjusted closes downloaded once this session for tickers not on disk (BTAL, DBMF, KMLM, AQMIX, ASFYX, PQTIX, MERFX, daily IEF, TLT, SPY, BIL, SHY, GLD). Fund survivorship: these are funds that still exist today; a composite of survivors flatters the sleeve and this is stated with every result that uses them.

T1_halloween.idea: Sell in May: hold SPY November-April, cash May-October (Bouman & Jacobsen, AER 2002; recalled, not read this session).
T1_halloween.sign: switch beats a constant mix with the same average equity exposure
T1_halloween.rule: monthly; 100% SPY in months Nov-Apr, 100% cash in May-Oct; 2 switches a year
T1_halloween.comparator: 50% SPY / 50% cash rebalanced monthly (same average exposure)
T1_halloween.window: decision window 2003-01 to 2026-08 (after publication); 1993-2002 reported as context only
T1_halloween.placebo: all 924 ways to pick 6 of 12 calendar months to hold SPY; exact rank of the Nov-Apr set by Sharpe
T1_halloween.pass: Sharpe difference vs comparator >= +0.10 AND placebo rank p < 0.0083 AND Sharpe difference > 0 in at least 3 of 4 regimes

T2_btal_sleeve.idea: An anti-beta fund (BTAL: long low-beta, short high-beta US stocks) as a crisis sleeve next to the benchmark.
T2_btal_sleeve.sign: 80% benchmark + 20% BTAL has a higher Sharpe and no deeper drawdown than the benchmark
comparators: 80% benchmark + 20% cash (the de-risking BTAL must beat, since a negative-beta fund is partly just less equity)
T2_btal_sleeve.pass: Sharpe difference vs BOTH comparators >= +0.05, bootstrap p < 0.0083 vs the benchmark, max drawdown no deeper than the benchmark's

T3_treasury_month_end.idea: Treasury returns concentrate in the last trading days of the month, from index-extension and rebalancing flows (Hartley & Schwarz, 'Predictable End-of-Month Treasury Returns', 2019; recalled, not read this session).
T3_treasury_month_end.sign: IEF earns more per day in the last 3 trading days of a month than on other days
T3_treasury_month_end.rule: buy IEF at the close of the 4th-to-last trading day, sell at the last close of the month; cash otherwise; 12 round trips a year
T3_treasury_month_end.window: design 2002-08 to 2018-12 (context); decision window 2019-01 to 2026-10 (after the paper)
T3_treasury_month_end.placebo: the same rule on every other 3-consecutive-trading-day slot counted from the month end (slots ending 3..18 days before month end); rank of the month-end slot
T3_treasury_month_end.pass: decision window: month-end slot mean excess return > 0 with t > 2.64 (p < 0.0083 two-sided normal) AND it ranks first among slots AND the strategy's excess return over cash is positive at 10 bps one-way
T3_treasury_month_end.also_reported: TLT, same rule, descriptive only, not a second trial

T4_rebalancing_bands.idea: Queue item B19. The allocation clocks reset weekly; a band or annual rule should cut trading with little change in risk.
T4_rebalancing_bands.rule: benchmark under four rules: weekly reset; monthly reset; annual reset (first week of January); 5-percentage-point absolute band (reset all three when any weight is more than 5pp from one third)
T4_rebalancing_bands.window: 2004-11 to 2026-09 weekly (full ETF panel history for GLD)
T4_rebalancing_bands.reading_fixed_in_advance: This is a cost and tax measurement, not an alpha test, so no significance test applies. A rule is RECOMMENDED over weekly reset if its annual turnover is at least 50% lower AND its Sharpe at 10 bps is within 0.03 AND its max drawdown is within 2 percentage points. Otherwise weekly reset stands.

T5_stacked_trend.idea: Capital-efficient ('return stacked') construction: keep 100% of the benchmark and add trend on top, instead of diluting the benchmark to 80% to make room. An individual gets this without borrowing through funds that hold futures internally.
T5_stacked_trend.rule: monthly; return = benchmark + 0.20 x (trend composite - cash) - 0.20 x 0.50%/yr financing and wrapper drag. Trend composite = equal weight of the managed-futures funds alive in each month among AQMIX, ASFYX, PQTIX, DBMF, KMLM (net of their own fees).
comparators: 80/20 unstacked (the trend_sleeve_8020_v1 design, with the same composite)
T5_stacked_trend.window: 2013-01 to 2026-10, the same post-publication start Step 340 used; already seen there for a different trend series
T5_stacked_trend.reading_fixed_in_advance: This is a risk-level and construction choice, not alpha: Step 340 already showed a 20% trend sleeve's Sharpe gain is not significant (p 0.24), and this trial cannot change that. SUPPORTED AS A CONSTRUCTION if, at 10 bps, CAGR is higher than the benchmark's AND Sharpe is not lower AND max drawdown is no deeper AND CAGR is higher than the unstacked 80/20's. The bootstrap p of the Sharpe difference vs the benchmark is reported and expected to fail 0.0083.
T5_stacked_trend.also_reported: single-fund (DBMF only) vs composite from 2019-06, descriptive, to show manager dispersion

T6_combination.idea: The brief's central question: does mixing several unrelated return streams beat the benchmark?
T6_combination.rule: monthly; weights proportional to 1 / trailing 36-month volatility, past data only (equal weight until 12 months exist), then blended with cash so that the trailing-36-month portfolio volatility matches the benchmark's trailing-36-month volatility, capped at 100% invested (no borrowing)
T6_combination.window: 2013-01 to 2026-10 (BTAL starts 2011-09; 12 months needed for the first weights)
T6_combination.pass: Sharpe difference vs the benchmark >= +0.10, bootstrap p < 0.0083, max drawdown no deeper, AND Sharpe difference > 0 in at least 3 of 4 regimes
T6_combination.also_reported: correlation matrix of the six sleeves, effective number of bets (eigenvalue entropy), leave-one-sleeve-out Sharpe, crisis windows 2020-02..03 and 2022
